body:
- Hype vs evidence: "ChatGPT beat the market by 70%" headlines come from months-long paper portfolios heavily tilted to AI/mega-cap winners (e.g., Nvidia concentration) during a strong tech run — a style/beta bet, not demonstrated skill.
- Most robust negative findings: overtrading/fees (Alpha Arena), concentration, hallucinated numbers without retrieval, look-ahead contamination in backtests. TradingAgents-style paper backtests on short windows are susceptible to the memorization problem.
- The defensible use case is analyst productivity (reading/summarizing/red-teaming primary documents with retrieval), not autonomous alpha.
- FinanceBench numbers are from 2023-era models; 2026 frontier models with long context are likely better, but no sourced current figure.

**Verified price block**
- Screener.in: **₹2,922**, stamped 19 Nov 2026 3:32 pm. Mcap ₹12,098 cr.
- 5paisa: ~₹2,908 (16 Nov, 2:16 pm; mcap ₹12,042 cr, P/E 45.8). Investing.com: ₹2,904.30 (16 Nov).
- **Price used: ~₹2,920.** The sources agree within 1%.
- Re-derived P/E: ₹12,098 / ₹263 cr TTM = **46.0×**. That is about 11.9× book.
- 52-week range ₹1,955–4,106 on screener; 5paisa shows a ₹2,121 low. The stock is **29% below its high**.
- Brokers: Citi Buy, target ₹3,300 (May-26). ICICI Securities Hold, target ₹2,800 (Jun-26).

**Financials (consolidated, ₹cr)**

| FY | Revenue | OPM | PAT | ROCE |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FY22 | 458 | 27% | 80 | 52% |
| FY23 | 617 | 29% | 117 | 51% |
| FY24 | 823 | 26% | 139 | 43% |
| FY25 | 1,133 | 26% | 196 | 44% |
| FY26 | 1,341 | 25% | 222 | 37% |
| TTM | 1,440 | 25% | 263 | 37.5% |

| Qtr | Mar-25 | Jun-25 | Sep-25 | Dec-25 | Mar-26 | Jun-26 | Sep-26 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | 283 | 294 | 320 | 343 | 361 | 348 | 389 |
| OPM | 24% | 23% | 23% | 23% | 26% | 26% | 26% |
| PAT | 52 | 52 | 54 | 58 | 59 | 75 | 72 |

There is no loss quarter. The Sep-26 PAT fell 4% QoQ because of an MTM loss on treasury income, which was ₹4 cr in other income vs ₹21 cr in Jun-26. The core operating profit was ₹102.8 cr, **up 42% YoY**.

**Balance sheet and holders.** Debt is ~₹40 cr, which is leases. CFO/PAT is 0.98 in FY26 and above 0.7 every year. Debtor days are 45–49, improving from 61–85. Equity is undiluted at ₹21 cr capital since FY22.

Shareholding:
- Promoter: flat at 55.31%. It fell 3.1% over 3 years from the Wargus/TA exit at listing.
- FII: 14.8% → 14.6%, flat.
- DII: 23.6% → 22.9%, flat.
- Retail shareholders jumped from 30.8k to 44.8k in Sep-26, so retail is chasing the dip. No pledge was found.

**Structural story and named cause.** Prudent is a B2B2C mutual fund distribution platform for ~30k+ sub-brokers in tier-2 and tier-3 towns. It is a direct way to own the *stock* of SIP savings rather than trading turnover, and its broking arm is small.
- Q2 FY27: quarterly average AUM **₹1.43 lakh cr**, up 21% YoY and 8% QoQ. Monthly SIP book ₹1,272 cr, up 17% YoY. Market share 3.7% vs 3.5%.
- OPM 26.4% vs 22.6% YoY. Management talks of "30%+ over time" from operating leverage.
- The step-change is real but modest, at 300 bp. It comes from **operating leverage and lower payout leakage, not mix**.
- SEBI's MF Regulations 2026 (TER restructuring, from 1 Apr 2026) were a headwind. A third-party estimate (Finology) puts the trail impact at ~2–3 bp, partly passed on to sub-brokers. Margins still expanded after the change, which is the evidence it was absorbed.

**Reverse DCF.** At 46×, the price implies **17–20% EPS CAGR for 10 years**. The 5-year PAT CAGR was 37% and the current YoY rate is ~34%, but SIP book growth is now only ~17% and industry SIP flows are flat MoM. **This is priced for continued excellence. It is not cheap.**

`case_study:evergrande-2021` | 2024-01-29 | tickers: HK-3333 | confidence: verified

Evergrande was the world's most indebted developer with ~$300 bn of liabilities (incl. presold apartments, supplier IOUs, wealth-management products sold to staff and the public). The stock rallied ~400%+ in 2017 to a peak ~HK$30 (Jul 2017-2018 area) and was suspended at ~HK$0.16 before delisting on 25 Aug 2025. Timeline: Aug 2020 Beijing's 'three red lines' (liability/assets ex-advances <70%, net gearing <100%, cash/short-term debt >1x) -- Evergrande failed all three; Sep 2021 missed payments and WMP protests; Dec 2021 offshore default; Jan 29 2024 Hong Kong court liquidation order; Mar 2024 CSRC found onshore unit Hengda inflated revenue by ~RMB 564 bn in 2019-2020 and fined founder Hui Ka Yan. Visible flags: (1) total liabilities growing faster than sales; heavy reliance on presales and commercial paper to suppliers; (2) perpetual bonds and high-yield offshore USD debt at 10%+; (3) large special dividends paid while highly levered; (4) diversification into EVs, football, bottled water; (5) contract assets/receivables and 'cash' that was restricted; (6) policy shift (three red lines) directly targeting its model. Lesson: when a sovereign changes rules aimed at your leverage model, exit; dividends paid out of borrowed money are a value-destruction signal. Liquidation recoveries for equity ~0.

**Lesson:** Policy aimed at your leverage = exit; equity in liquidation ~0
**Spotted early by:** credit markets (offshore bond yields), short sellers; policy watchers

`case_study:pidilite-2008-2026` · tickers: PIDILITIND · confidence: single-source

Split/bonus-adjusted ₹19.8 (Oct 2008) → ₹1,231 (Dec 2021) ≈62x; ₹1,580 on 19 Nov 2026 (≈80x; ATH ₹1,693 Aug 2026). 2008–21 twin engine: P/E 15.7 → 93 (5.9x) × implied EPS ~10.5x, so about 43% of the log-return was rerating. Max drawdown after 2008 only −26%/−27% (2020, 2022), the shallowest in this library; 2008 itself was −61%. Early signal (general knowledge, unverified narrative): near-monopoly consumer adhesives (Fevicol, M-Seal, Fevikwik) with pricing power; when VAM input prices collapsed in late 2008 margins jumped (screener OPM 16% FY15 → 22% FY16) while the stock was at ~15x. Promoter holding ~69–70% steady. Investors were 'coffee-can' holders. Stall: Dec 2021 → Nov 2026 EPS doubled (₹13.2 → ₹26.4) but P/E fell 93 → 60, so the price rose only ~28% in ~5 years. Lesson: a true moat gives shallow drawdowns and steady EPS, but even the best franchise had a P/E ceiling near 90–100 in India; returns after that point track EPS minus de-rating.

Key data: **start_year**: 2008; **end_year**: 2026; **start_price**: 19.8; **end_price**: 1580; **multiple**: ~80x (62x to 2021); **pe_start**: 15.7; **pe_end_2021**: 93.0; **pe_nov2026**: 60.0; **eps_multiple_implied**: ~10.5x (2008-21); **max_drawdown**: -27% after 2008; **early_signals**: input-cost collapse 2008-09 + pricing power, at 15x; **ended**: not ended; returns slowed after P/E 93 in 2021; **lesson**: moats reduce drawdowns, not valuation risk

Sources: <https://www.screener.in/company/PIDILITIND/consolidated/>
